title: `MainLoop`-derived scripts break if there's a static variable in it
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5.1.stable, 4.6.dev [757bba192ef4c3254b44bc0d2c8cf36aa3343e30]

### System information

Godot v4.6.dev (757bba192) - Fedora Linux 42 (Adams) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (RADV GFX1201) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 60.39 GiB memory

### Issue description

When using a custom `MainLoop` (as set through the `application/run/main_loop_type` project setting) written in GDScript, with any sort of static member, like so:

```gdscript
class_name MyMainLoop
extends SceneTree

static var my_static_member := 42
```

... you end up getting a ton of these errors when running the game:

```
E 0:00:00:508   my_main_loop.gd:5 @ @static_initializer(): Parameter "SceneTree::get_singleton()" is null.
  <C++ Source>  scene/debugger/scene_debugger.cpp:506 @ parse_message()
  <Stack Trace> my_main_loop.gd:5 @ @static_initializer()
```

These errors seem to pretty much break the script/instance in general as well, as anything connecting to `SceneTree` signals no longer seem to function after these errors have been emitted. One example of this are the signals that are used by `RuntimeNodeSelect` for the remote selection in the embedded game window:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d743736f84fb668bcdfb5bf86258e483f35c6fec/scene/debugger/scene_debugger.cpp#L1641-L1642

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the MRP
1. Run the main scene using the embedded game window
1. Note the errors about `SceneTree::get_singleton()` being null
1. Switch to the "2D" selection mode in the embedded game window toolbar
1. Try and select one of the `ColorRect`
1. Note how no selection happens

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[gdscript_main_loop_static_error_2025-12-10_18-36-58.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24085012/gdscript_main_loop_static_error_2025-12-10_18-36-58.zip)
